natural and degraded open areas, palm savanna, sandbanks and various grasslands from southwestern Nicaragua southeastward to northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward in interior Colombia to the headwaters of the Río Cauca and Río Magdalena and south along the Pacific lowlands to southwestern Colombia; east of the Andes from northern and central Venezuela, Trinidad and Tobago, and the Guianas southward across most Amazon River basin to northern Bolivia, especially along major rivers, and in interior and eastern Brazil southward to northeastern Argentina and northern Uruguay

Distribution and habitat: — Aspalathus chlorina is a colonial reseeder that habituates northern moderate slopes in Kouga Grassy Sandstone Fynbos (FFs 28, Rebelo et al. 2006) of the Baviaanskloof Biosphere Reserve (Fig. 2). It is known from two localised populations each comprising a few hundred plants in the Kouga mountains at about 580 – 600 m.
